description: Grounding check for RAG answers: does the cited passage actually support the claim.

supported.instructions: Does `passage` support `claim`: would a careful reader agree the claim follows from the passage alone? Faithful paraphrase and plain arithmetic on the passage's numbers are fine. Claims that go beyond, contradict, or change numbers, dates, certainty or scope are not supported.

criteria.false: Not supported: contradicted, overstated, or absent

state.passage: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889 for the World's Fair in Paris.
state.claim: The Eiffel Tower was finished in 1889.

state.passage: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889 for the World's Fair in Paris.
state.claim: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1899.

state.passage: In the trial, 62% of patients receiving the drug improved, compared with 48% on placebo.
state.claim: Most patients on the drug improved.

state.passage: In the trial, 62% of patients receiving the drug improved, compared with 48% on placebo.
state.claim: The drug cures the condition.

state.passage: Revenue rose 12% year over year, while operating costs grew 15%.
state.claim: Operating margin improved.

cases.rationale: Costs grew faster than revenue, so operating margin fell: claim contradicted.

state.passage: The library supports Python 3.10 and later. Python 3.9 reached end of life and is no longer tested.
state.claim: The library does not officially support Python 3.9.

state.passage: Copenhagen's metro opened in 2002 and runs 24 hours a day.
state.claim: Copenhagen has the oldest metro in Scandinavia.

state.passage: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week with manager approval.
state.claim: Remote work requires manager approval.

state.passage: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week with manager approval.
state.claim: Employees can work fully remote.

state.passage: The study followed 1,200 adults in Denmark for ten years and found no link between coffee intake and heart disease.
state.claim: A Danish study found coffee does not raise heart disease risk.

state.passage: The API returns HTTP 429 when the client exceeds 80 requests per second.
state.claim: The API rate limit is 100 requests per second.

state.passage: The bridge was closed for repairs from March to June; traffic was diverted via the ring road.
state.claim: The bridge was closed for about three months.

cases.rationale: March to June is roughly three months.

state.passage: Medarbejdere har ret til fem ugers betalt ferie om året.
state.claim: Employees get five weeks of paid vacation per year.

state.passage: Medarbejdere har ret til fem ugers betalt ferie om året.
state.claim: Employees get six weeks of paid vacation per year.

state.passage: Version 4.0 removed the deprecated `connect()` helper. Users should call `Client.open()` instead. The old helper had been deprecated since 3.2 and printed a warning on every call. Migration notes are in MIGRATING.md, which also covers the renamed configuration keys and the new default timeout of 30 seconds, up from 10 seconds in 3.x.
state.claim: In 4.0 the default timeout went from 10 to 30 seconds and connect() was removed.

state.passage: Version 4.0 removed the deprecated `connect()` helper. Users should call `Client.open()` instead. The old helper had been deprecated since 3.2 and printed a warning on every call. Migration notes are in MIGRATING.md, which also covers the renamed configuration keys and the new default timeout of 30 seconds, up from 10 seconds in 3.x.
state.claim: connect() was deprecated in 4.0 and will be removed in 5.0.

state.passage: Early results suggest the vaccine may reduce hospitalizations in adults over 65.
state.claim: The vaccine reduces hospitalizations in adults over 65.

cases.rationale: Removes the hedge ('suggest ... may'), raising certainty beyond the passage.

state.passage: The update will most likely ship in November, though the date could still slip.
state.claim: The update ships in November.

cases.rationale: Turns a likely date the passage says could slip into a certainty.

state.passage: The museum is open Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00. Admission is free for children under 12.
state.claim: The museum is open every day, and children under 12 get in free.

cases.rationale: The second half is supported but 'every day' contradicts Tuesday to Sunday, so the claim as a whole is not.

state.passage: Of the 40 people surveyed, 30 said they cycle to work.
state.claim: Three quarters of respondents commute by bike.

cases.rationale: Low word overlap, but 30 of 40 is three quarters: plain arithmetic and paraphrase.

state.passage: The board discussed the proposal to move the headquarters to Aarhus and will vote on it in January.
state.claim: The board voted to move the headquarters to Aarhus.

cases.rationale: High overlap, but the vote has not happened yet.

state.passage: Ticket sales stopped on 3 May because every seat in the 2,000-seat hall had been sold.
state.claim: The event sold out.

cases.rationale: Every seat sold is a faithful paraphrase of selling out.

state.passage: Regeringen overvejer at hæve pensionsalderen til 70 år fra 2040.
state.claim: The pension age will be raised to 70 from 2040.

cases.rationale: The government is only considering it; the claim states it as decided.

state.passage: In the pilot, 61 UK companies tested a four-day week; 56 of them kept it after the trial ended.
state.claim: Most companies in the pilot kept the four-day week.

cases.rationale: 56 of 61 is most: plain arithmetic on the passage.

state.passage: The city council approved the new cycling plan on 12 September by 21 votes to 10. The plan adds 38 kilometres of protected bike lanes over five years, starting with the ring road and the harbour front in 2027. It is funded by a combination of the municipal budget and a state infrastructure grant of 140 million kroner, which covers roughly half of the total cost. Car parking on the affected streets will be reduced by about 600 spaces, and the council has asked the administration to propose replacement parking in two new garages before construction starts. The opposition argued that the plan should have been put to a public vote, but a proposal for a referendum was rejected. Businesses on the harbour front will be consulted on delivery access during spring 2026, and the first construction contracts are expected to be tendered in the autumn of that year.
state.claim: The plan adds 38 km of protected bike lanes and is fully funded by a state grant.

cases.rationale: The first fact is supported, but the grant covers roughly half the cost, not all of it.

state.passage: The city council approved the new cycling plan on 12 September by 21 votes to 10. The plan adds 38 kilometres of protected bike lanes over five years, starting with the ring road and the harbour front in 2027. It is funded by a combination of the municipal budget and a state infrastructure grant of 140 million kroner, which covers roughly half of the total cost. Car parking on the affected streets will be reduced by about 600 spaces, and the council has asked the administration to propose replacement parking in two new garages before construction starts. The opposition argued that the plan should have been put to a public vote, but a proposal for a referendum was rejected. Businesses on the harbour front will be consulted on delivery access during spring 2026, and the first construction contracts are expected to be tendered in the autumn of that year.
state.claim: A majority of the council backed the plan, and a referendum on it was turned down.

cases.rationale: 21 to 10 is a majority and the referendum proposal was rejected: both parts follow.
